guides.title: Fix macOS Wi-Fi That Keeps Disconnecting or Dropping
guides.symptom: My Mac Wi-Fi drops randomly, shows an exclamation mark, or won't connect after sleep
guides.description: Diagnose and resolve intermittent Wi-Fi drops, DHCP lease failures, and corrupted network configuration files on Mac.
causes: Corrupted airport and network preference plist files in SystemConfiguration
Expired or conflicting DHCP lease from the router
Private Wi-Fi Address MAC randomization creating handshake collisions with specific routers
guides.whyItWorks: macOS stores network interface profiles in `/Library/Preferences/SystemConfiguration/`. Removing these corrupted plist files forces macOS to reconstruct fresh network interfaces. Renewing the DHCP lease forces a clean IP assignment from the router.

steps.detail: Open Apple menu () > System Settings > Wi-Fi. Click 'Details...' next to your connected Wi-Fi network. In the sidebar, select 'TCP/IP'. Click the 'Renew DHCP Lease' button, then click OK. This refreshes your IP address without disconnecting.

steps.instruction: Disable Private Wi-Fi Address for troublesome home/work routers
steps.detail: In System Settings > Wi-Fi > Details... next to your network, look for 'Private Wi-Fi address'. Set it to 'Off'. Some mesh Wi-Fi systems and corporate routers disconnect devices whose MAC address rotates periodically.

steps.instruction: Flush macOS DNS cache via Terminal
steps.detail:
Open Terminal (Cmd+Space, type Terminal) and run:
sudo dscacheutil -flushcache; sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder
Enter your administrator password. This clears poisoned or stalled domain lookups.

Open Finder, press Cmd+Shift+G and paste:
/Library/Preferences/SystemConfiguration/
Find and move these files to Trash (or a backup folder):
- com.apple.airport.preferences.plist
- com.apple.network.identification.plist
- NetworkInterfaces.plist
- preferences.plist
Restart your Mac. macOS will automatically regenerate clean network configuration files on boot.
steps.warning: This requires admin privileges and will reset your saved Wi-Fi networks and VPN profiles. You will need to re-enter your Wi-Fi password after restart.

guides.title: Fix Spinning Beach Ball of Death & Slow Mac Performance
guides.symptom: Mac freezes frequently, apps stop responding, or the spinning color wheel appears constantly
guides.description: Troubleshoot system freezes, track memory pressure in Activity Monitor, and disable resource-hogging background startup items.
causes: Memory pressure reaching the red zone, causing aggressive disk swapping
Runaway background processes (such as mdworker indexing or web helper threads)
Too many heavy Login Items launching automatically at boot
guides.whyItWorks: The spinning beach ball indicates that an application's main thread event loop is blocked. Activity Monitor reveals whether the bottleneck is CPU starvation or RAM exhaustion (measured by macOS memory pressure). Killing locked processes and removing startup daemons restores fluid responsiveness.

steps.instruction: Open Activity Monitor and inspect CPU and Memory Pressure
steps.detail: Press Cmd+Space, type 'Activity Monitor', and press Return. Click the '% CPU' column header to sort descending. If an app is at 100%+ or shows in red as '(Not Responding)', select it and click the (X) button at the top > 'Force Quit'. Next, check the 'Memory' tab: look at the 'Memory Pressure' graph at the bottom. Green is healthy; yellow/red means you are out of RAM.

steps.instruction: Prune Login Items and Allow in Background daemons
steps.detail: Go to Apple menu () > System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions. Under 'Open at Login', select unnecessary apps (like Spotify, Steam, Discord) and click the minus (-) button. Under 'Allow in the Background', turn off toggles for updaters and tools you do not actively need running 24/7.

Click Apple () > Restart... Uncheck 'Reopen windows when logging back in' and click Restart. A fresh restart clears out memory leaks in graphics and window rendering daemons (WindowServer) that accumulate over weeks of continuous uptime.

guides.title: Fix Mac Printer Showing Offline or Paused (Reset CUPS)
guides.symptom: Printer won't print from Mac, prints stay in queue, or printer status says 'Paused'
guides.description: Unjam stuck print queues, reset the macOS CUPS printing subsystem, and re-add network or AirPrint printers.
causes: Stuck print spool job locking the CUPS daemon
Outdated third-party printer driver incompatible with current macOS version
guides.whyItWorks: macOS handles all printing through CUPS (Common Unix Printing System). Resetting the printing system flushes all print queues, deletes corrupt driver caches, and restores default CUPS configuration files.

steps.detail: Open Apple menu () > System Settings > Printers & Scanners. Click on your printer and click 'Open Print Queue...'. If the toolbar shows a 'Resume' button with a play icon, click it. Select any stuck documents in the list and click the (X) delete button.

In System Settings > Printers & Scanners, Control-click (or right-click) anywhere in the Printers list (or on your printer name). Select 'Reset Printing System...'. Confirm the prompt and enter your administrator password. This will wipe all queues and printer settings clean.
steps.warning: Resetting the printing system removes all installed printers and scanners. You will need to re-add your printer.

steps.instruction: Re-add printer using AirPrint or updated drivers
steps.detail: Click 'Add Printer, Scanner, or Fax...'. Select your printer when it appears on the local network or USB. Under 'Use:', make sure 'AirPrint' or 'Secure AirPrint' is chosen (which doesn't require third-party drivers) whenever possible. Click Add.
